questions.prompt: Why does the time go into a user message at the end of the history, not into a prompt section?
options: The model cannot read times in the system prompt
A changing system prompt would change the request start and lose the cache hit
User messages are cheaper per token than system messages
questions.explanation: The system prompt sits at the start of every request. Adding the fact at the end keeps every earlier byte the same, so the prefix cache still matches.

questions.prompt: Step 2 of a turn starts 5 seconds after step 1, which got a time note. What does the listener do?
options: It adds a new time note
It adds nothing, because less than 600,000 ms passed
It throws, because two steps are too close
questions.explanation: The listener only adds a note when the last one is at least 600,000 ms (10 minutes) old. 5 seconds is far less.

questions.prompt: Why does the loop append each time note to the record as a user/message event?
options: So any request the model saw can be rebuilt from the record
So the person sees the time in the chat
So the note is sent twice
So the next step can delete it
questions.explanation: Anything the model sees must first be written to the record. A logged note lets a reader rebuild the exact request.
